item.title: Government spent $10 million on pro-Trump ads after president said super PAC would fund
item.description: Nearly $22 million in taxpayers funds has been spent to air the ads, with nearly half spent after Trump promised to fund what the White House calls public service announcements through his super PAC.

item.title: Actor Selma Blair removed from plane by police after altercation
item.description: Authorities say Blair was physically abusive and injured two flight attendants while traveling from Los Angeles to New York. A Blair representative said she had a medical emergency aboard the plane.

item.title: U.S. restrictions on Chinese drones are hurting cash-strapped police departments
item.description: The U.S. government is trying to end the dominance of high-quality, low-cost drones made in China. But more restrictions mean higher costs for cash-strapped police forces that rely on those drones.

item.title: Yale Law expert on Hegseth's plans to livestream execution
item.description: Military justice expert Eugene Fidell of Yale Law School speaks to NPR about the Pentagon's plan to livestream the execution of a convicted mass murderer.

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel downgraded as high winds and rain turn inward
item.description: Forecasters say the storm, which brought heavy rain and coastal flooding, is a preview of what may be in store as California braces for a possibly record-setting El Niño.

item.title: How Trump reshaped the DOJ's Civil Rights Division to serve his agenda
item.description: The Civil Rights Division, long the crown jewel of the Justice Department, has been radically reshaped under President Trump, using its enforcement powers to pursue the president's MAGA agenda.

item.title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
item.description: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.
